PIQA supplies historical background on physical-commonsense limitations. Its older models cannot establish contemporary performance or unchanged error rates.
Documents contemporary reasoning improvements on different tasks. Relative gains do not establish reliable everyday commonsense reasoning.

reviews.rationale: SimpleToM demonstrates systematic commonsense-dependent failures across leading contemporary models, and PIQA supplies the historical background. Successful subtasks, o1's gains, and tailored prompting improvements do not negate persistent unreliability. The evidence does not establish an error rate across all real-world uses.

reviews.rationale: GSM-Plus supports the claimed tendency through paired original and altered questions. Numerical and wording resilience and successful prompting improvements do not contradict occasional failures. Baseline accuracy supports the contract's familiarity proxy without proving uncontaminated generalization.
